analysis.title: "Unplayable": Goldman's Molavi Says Anyone Carrying Gross Lost Money As Momentum Moves More Violent Than 2000, 2009, Or 2020
key_insights: Molavi calls the last two to three weeks "unplayable". The S&P 500 is near its record high, but anyone carrying gross lost money across regions, strategies and gross, net or skew exposure. Cash was the only place to hide.

The AI unwind, de-grossing and performance pain produced large factor, sector, spread and theme volatility. The Nasdaq is down over 6% in two weeks, semis sold off sharply, and momentum is down about 15% over the same period.
Goldman's Broad AI basket relative to the S&P ex-AI has suffered its second 20%+ drawdown since peaking earlier this year (as of Oct 23).
Oct 22 was the 5th largest de-grossing event this year, driven entirely by long selling. It was the largest long selling since September 2025, so owners were exiting rather than shorts pressing.

US Quality is at 12-month highs after one of its strongest periods of outperformance, even with the 10Y yield above 5.2% (as of Oct 13). Rotation is into defensive, real assets, quality and low leverage names.
Cyclicals vs defensives in both the US and Europe have rolled over alongside the momentum unwind.
US momentum vs the market has given back all of its 2026 gains, after being up roughly 25% at the June peak. Goldman's momentum pair is about 43% below its high, just above its August low.

Goldman's momentum pair has had 30 sessions in 2026 with a move of 5% or more, versus 23 in 2000, 16 in 2009 and 21 in 2020. The average VIX over 2026 is 18.1, versus 23.3 in 2000, 31.5 in 2009 and 29.3 in 2020.

Macro backdrop: Middle East anxiety is pushing oil back toward its April/May highs, French social unrest has pushed OAT-Bund spreads to all-time highs, and yields are falling on AI unwind and slower capex concerns rather than being welcomed.
Fed hike probability has fallen from near certainty to around 75% over the last couple of weeks, per Molavi.
Earnings have been very solid with little to no reward. Meta ramping capex and Tesla cutting capex both sold off, so the market is treating spending and austerity the same.
Molavi calls the Meta news (an equity raise of up to $95B, with Meta's chip suppliers buying in after the debt window closed) a potential clearing event that gives room to breathe.

Breadth is the silver lining: the share of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average rose 5 points Friday to 61%, the highest since August, and is up 17 points in three weeks while the index went nowhere. Molavi sees the unwind as a clean-out of positioning, lower concentration and multiple normalisation.
Seasonality: in 30 years November has had only three S&P drawdowns (Nov 2000 -8%, Nov 2007 -4.4%, Nov 2008 -7.48%).

Molavi's conclusion is that investors are playing defense and it feels closer to the end than the beginning, with vol normalization the first step. People are waiting for a bottom to become self-evident rather than calling it.

ZeroHedge's own view is that a positioning flush does not fix a funding problem and the index may have catching up to do, with factor volatility at crisis levels under an 18 VIX, French spreads at records and the Fed leaning toward a hike.

A semis rout and a second 20%+ drawdown in the Broad AI basket relative to the S&P ex-AI, plus stress in AI-linked credit instruments.

Quality rallied even with yields this high, so rates offered no support. Yields have since retraced.
Social unrest in France is widening spreads.
Renewed Middle East anxiety is pushing oil higher.
Far below the 23.3 (2000), 31.5 (2009) and 29.3 (2020) averages despite higher momentum volatility.
The highest since August, up 5 points on Friday and 17 points over three weeks.

risk_factors: A positioning flush does not fix AI funding stress. The buildout has moved from who wants to lend to who wants to dilute, and Meta is raising up to $95B of equity after the debt window closed.
Oil rising toward its April/May highs on Middle East anxiety.
French social unrest and record OAT-Bund spreads.
The Fed may still hike, with about 75% probability priced.
A weak November: red tends to signal very red to follow. Past November drawdowns came in 2000, 2007 and 2008.
No one is willing to call a bottom, and the lack of conviction and performance buffer keeps flow-driven volatility high.
Slower AI capex weighs on GDP via a smaller AI tailwind.
